Immigration Issues & Resources in the Sixth District | Congresswoman April McClain Delaney Skip to main content Immigration Issues & Resources in the Sixth District Immigration Issues & Resources in the Sixth District Congresswoman McClain Delaney is staunchly opposed to the unlawful, inhumane actions taken by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement since the beginning of the Trump Administration’s second term. Aggressive immigration enforcement actions have hurt communities throughout the nation, including those in the Sixth District and across Maryland. She is fighting in Congress for commonsense reforms to immigration enforcement. Know Your Rights It is important that all U.S. citizens and immigrants (regardless of legal status)  know their rights when interacting with law enforcement or Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents. We have a  'Know Your Rights' resource to help you navigate interactions with ICE agents and legal resources. We also have  bilingual palm cards that can be printed and carried with you that provide translated instructions to law enforcement officers. These resources are available in six languages: English, Spanish, Chinese (Traditional and Simplified), Korean, French, and Farsi.   Image   Need Help with an Immigration Issue?  Our office is dedicated to help Sixth District constituents navigate issues with federal agencies on topics such as passports, citizenship, green cards, work permits, and more. We can inquire and advocate on a constituent’s behalf to check on statuses, expedite service, find solutions, and try to cut through red tape.  Learn how we can help you . If you or a loved one has been detained by ICE, we want to hear from you immediately–and know that we take your confidentiality seriously.  Please call or visit our offices in Washington, D.C. or in Downtown Frederick. ICE’s Planned Detention Warehouse   Image   The Congresswoman is vehemently opposed to ICE’s plans for a 1,500-bed detention warehouse in Washington County. Know Your Rights - Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Maryland’s 6th | Congresswoman April McClain Delaney Skip to main content Know Your Rights - Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Maryland’s 6th Across the country and in Maryland’s 6th District, it is important to know your rights when interacting with law enforcement or Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents. In the United States, immigrants are entitled to their fundamental rights under the Constitution—rights that must be protected. Your local congressional office has the power to request information and check on the status of open cases with any federal agency. Our office can be reached at 301-926-0300 , and our official website is https://mcclaindelaney.house.gov/ . Our office has provided  resources outlining your basic rights while you are physically in the United States and precautionary measures you may choose to take. In addition to English, these resources are available in five additional languages, including: Spanish ( Guide ,  Palm Card )  French ( Guide ,  Palm Card )  Chinese Traditional ( Guide ,  Palm Card )  Simplified ( Guide ,  Palm Card )  Korean ( Guide ,  Palm Card )  Farsi ( Guide ,  Palm Card )  Legal disclaimer: These resources are for general informational purposes only. Its contents are not legal advice. En todo el país y en el Sexto Distrito de Maryland, es importante conocer sus derechos al interactuar con las fuerzas del orden o con agentes del Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE). En los Estados Unidos, las personas inmigrantes tienen derecho a sus derechos fundamentales bajo la Constitución—derechos que deben ser protegidos. Su oficina congresional local tiene la autoridad para solicitar información y verificar el estado de casos abiertos con cualquier agencia federal. Puede comunicarse con nuestra oficina al 301-926-0300 , y visitar nuestro sitio web oficial en https://mcclaindelaney.house.gov/ . McClain Delaney, Van Hollen, Alsobrooks Announce Over $560,000 for Workforce Development, Supportive Housing in Western Maryland | Congresswoman April McClain Delaney Skip to main content McClain Delaney, Van Hollen, Alsobrooks Announce Over $560,000 for Workforce Development, Supportive Housing in Western Maryland Wednesday, August 5, 2026 WASHINGTON – Today, Congresswoman April McClain Delaney and U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (all D-Md.) announced $562,851 in federal funding from the Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) for education, workforce development, and supportive housing for adults recovering from mental illness or with developmental disabilities in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington Counties.   “Western Maryland is full of talent and potential, and these federal investments will help turn that potential into opportunity,”  said Congresswoman McClain Delaney.  “This funding will expand research and student training at Frostburg’s Appalachian Lab, prepare Garrett College students for good-paying welding jobs, and provide stable housing and employment support through Archway Station. I’ll keep fighting to bring home resources that strengthen our rural communities.”   “When we invest in opportunities for education, workforce training, and supportive housing, we invest in the long-term success of our communities. These federal dollars from the Appalachian Regional Commission will help create educational opportunities, open pathways to good-paying jobs, and strengthen the financial stability of Marylanders,”  said Senator Van Hollen.   “When we invest in Western Maryland, our entire state benefits. This federal investment will support research at the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science’s Appalachian Lab in Frostburg, create more opportunities for Marylanders developing their careers at Garrett College’s Career Technology Training Center, and renovate critical housing for adults recovering from mental illness or developmental disabilities. McClain Delaney & Obernolte, Led Bipartisan Letter to the Department of State, Department of Commerce, and Federal Communications Commission Requesting Update on U.S. Strategy for the World Radio Conference 2027 | Congresswoman April McClain Delaney Skip to main content Reps. McClain Delaney & Obernolte, Led Bipartisan Letter to the Department of State, Department of Commerce, and Federal Communications Commission Requesting Update on U.S. Strategy for the World Radio Conference 2027 Tuesday, July 28, 2026 WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last week, Representatives April McClain Delaney (MD-06) and Jay Obernolte (CA-23) led a bipartisan  letter , joined by 17 House colleagues, requesting that the Department of State, Department of Commerce, and Federal Communications Commission provide Congress with a written update on U.S. strategy for the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference (WRC-27), including how agencies are coordinating, structuring leadership, and engaging internationally to protect U.S. spectrum priorities. The letter, sent to Under Secretary of State Jacob Helberg, NTIA Administrator Arielle Roth, and FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, highlights the significance of the decisions that will be made at WRC-27, which will be hosted in Shanghai, China. It underscores the importance of preserving global momentum for unlicensed 6 GHz access, a critical driver of U.S. innovation, Wi-Fi leadership, and long-term economic competitiveness, as the PRC and aligned countries push to redefine global spectrum standards. "As other nations, including the People's Republic of China, work to shape global spectrum policy, the United States must lead—not react. Strong coordination across our federal agencies and close collaboration with our allies are essential to protecting American innovation, strengthening our economic competitiveness, and ensuring the technologies that power our homes, businesses, and communities continue to be built on U.S. leadership,”  said Congresswoman April McClain Delaney .  “ We applaud the House members, led by Reps.
